messages:
incident-bot: Pager: dedicated-resv-pool-exhaustion triggered for pool="resv-east-1". queue_size=1124, avg_wait_s=612, severity=P1. Affected tenants: AcmeCorp (reserved), NovaHealth (reserved). Auto-scale attempts failing. Paging oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: ACK — jumping on it. grabbing initial cluster metrics.

maria (customer-sre): FYI support: AcmeCorp reporting 429s and elevated latency. Ticket #INC-12345 opened. They see model timeouts in their prod requests.

cheng (eng-runtime): Quick check: KV cache memory for resv-east-1 nodes at 98%. We have a backlog of long-lived sessions from a single tenant. Could be noisy neighbor.

sam (platform-oncall): Autoscaler logs show repeated 429/503 from cloud API when requesting additional GPUs — looks like provider rate-limit/quota. Example: 
```
2026-03-17T02:12:04Z ERROR autoscaler: scale_up failed: ProviderError 429 RateExceeded
request_id=abc123 quota_remaining=0
```

kate (ops-manager): Can we run an emergency reclaim/eviction to free capacity? Need to coordinate with support for customer impact messaging.

cheng (eng-runtime): Recommend preemptive eviction of low-priority sessions + enforce per-tenant concurrency caps. I can trigger eviction via ops endpoint:
```bash
curl -X POST https://ops.internal/api/v1/pools/resv-east-1/evict \ 
  -d '{"percent": 12, "criteria": "age>3600,priority=low"}' \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_API'
```

oncall-sre: Running eviction now (manual approval). Will post progress.

incident-bot: Action started: preemptive-eviction id=evict-1713004321 user=oncall-sre percent=12

alex (devex): Heads-up: evicting will disrupt long-running batch jobs for tenants without burst protection. Notify AcmeCorp support thread.

maria (customer-sre): Notifying AcmeCorp now — will include ETA and mitigation steps.

15m later — oncall-sre: eviction completed. reclaimed 12 GPUs (approx). queue_size dropped from 1124 -> 342. avg_wait_s now 210.

sam (platform-oncall): Autoscaler still failing to scale due to provider quota. Filed cloud support case CAS-98765. In parallel we should route critical enterprise traffic to fallback pool resv-west-1.

cheng (eng-runtime): Routing plan: temporary weighted route for reserved tenants. Command: 
```bash
rbctl route set --tenant AcmeCorp --from-pool resv-east-1 --to-pool resv-west-1 --weight 100 --reason "emergency failover"
```

oncall-sre: Applying route for AcmeCorp now.

maria (customer-sre): AcmeCorp confirms they can accept transient region failover. Support updated.

kate (ops-manager): Noise analysis — which tenant caused cache bloat?

cheng (eng-runtime): Found one heavy session pattern from tenant id=acme-batch that is holding many KV shards and lots of long prefix keys. Suggest adding per-tenant kv_limit and session TTL policy:
```yaml
tenant_caps:
  acme-batch:
    concurrency: 8
    kv_keys_limit: 50000
    session_ttl_s: 3600
```

alex (devex): I'll draft a post-incident note and suggested customer-facing blurb for support.

oncall-sre: Queue trending: 342 -> 128 over next 9m after route + eviction. Throttles reduced.

sam (platform-oncall): Cloud provider responded: temporary quota lift requested, ETA ~2h. Meanwhile we have failover in place.

maria (customer-sre): NovaHealth noticed degraded quality in fallback region (model versions mismatch). We routed only traffic that tolerates fallback; still some customers affected. Logging for regression.

kate (ops-manager): Good containment. Next steps: (1) postmortem to include autoscaler retry/backoff logic and provider quota handling, (2) add alert for autoscaler provider-429 spike, (3) add per-tenant eviction policies and kv limits, (4) review reserved-pool headroom policy.

cheng (eng-runtime): Will open tasks for runtime limits + ops endpoint to preview eviction impact. Also adding a lighter-weight per-tenant throttle so single tenant can't saturate pool.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> partial (failover active, autoscaler pending quota). start_ts=1713004321.

oncall-sre: marking as whiteboarded/handed to day team. I'll hand off to oncall rotation at 08:00 local.

kate (ops-manager): Escalation note: follow up with cloud account team re: quota and request permanent increase for resv-east-1 reserved GPU pool.

alex (devex): Draft of customer blurb: "We experienced temporary capacity exhaustion in our East reserved GPU pool causing throttling for some enterprise tenants. We applied emergency eviction and routed critical traffic to a fallback pool. Autoscaler requests to the cloud were rate-limited; working with provider. We are adding protections to prevent recurrence."

maria (customer-sre): Sent update to AcmeCorp + NovaHealth, both acknowledged.

incident-bot: Incident update posted to #incidents-digest. last_update_ts=1713005567.

kate (ops-manager): Closing short-term incident thread. Follow-ups assigned. Thanks team. :tada:
